request: How large is the immigration court backlog and how has it changed over time?

reply.reply:
**The immigration court backlog reached 3,558,995 pending cases at the end of FY2024, after surpassing 1 million in FY2019 and continuing to grow.**

- At the end of FY2024, EOIR had 3,558,995 pending immigration court cases. (IN12492, PDF p. 4)
- Immigration court caseloads have generally increased since 1983, with annual receipts rising more significantly since FY2019 except during FY2020 and FY2021. (IN12492, PDF p. 2)
- Pending immigration court cases surpassed 1 million in FY2019 and rose to 1,405,386 million by the end of FY2021, according to the report. (R47077, PDF p. 21)
reply.reasoning: The newest CRS report provides the FY2024 total and describes long-term growth in receipts; an earlier CRS report gives the FY2019 threshold and FY2021 snapshot. Note: the FY2021 source sentence prints “1,405,386 million,” which appears internally inconsistent, so the headline relies on the verified FY2024 total and qualitative trend.
